claims.title: Battle of the Golden Spurs
claims.summary: A Flemish town militia, mostly craft guildsmen, destroyed a French army of knights near Courtrai, collecting the golden spurs of the slain nobles and asserting the independence of the Flemish towns.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Belgium: From the cloth towns of Flanders to the heart of Europe, a young kingdom carved from the old Low Countries.", terralore.co/country/BEL/chronicle#ev-1302-battle-of-the-golden-spurs, claim TL:BEL:event:1302:battle-of-the-golden-spurs, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Flemish cloth boom
claims.summary: Importing English wool, Bruges, Ghent and Ypres became among the richest cloth-producing cities in Europe, with Bruges the leading port and financial centre of the north.

sources.label: Rise and Fall of the Medieval Flemish Cloth Industry

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Belgium: From the cloth towns of Flanders to the heart of Europe, a young kingdom carved from the old Low Countries.", terralore.co/country/BEL/chronicle#ev-1200-the-flemish-cloth-boom, claim TL:BEL:event:1200:the-flemish-cloth-boom, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Foundation of the beguinages
claims.summary: Communities of beguines, women living a religious life without taking monastic vows, established enclosed beguinages in the Flemish towns; thirteen survive as a UNESCO World Heritage site bearing witness to this medieval tradition.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Belgium: From the cloth towns of Flanders to the heart of Europe, a young kingdom carved from the old Low Countries.", terralore.co/country/BEL/chronicle#ev-1245-foundation-of-the-beguinages, claim TL:BEL:event:1245:foundation-of-the-beguinages, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Flanders passes to Burgundy
claims.summary: On the death of the last count, the County of Flanders was inherited by Philip the Bold, Duke of Burgundy, beginning the gathering of the Low Countries under a single dynasty.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Belgium: From the cloth towns of Flanders to the heart of Europe, a young kingdom carved from the old Low Countries.", terralore.co/country/BEL/chronicle#ev-1384-flanders-passes-to-burgundy, claim TL:BEL:event:1384:flanders-passes-to-burgundy, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Habsburg inheritance
claims.summary: After Charles the Bold of Burgundy was killed, his daughter Mary married the Habsburg archduke Maximilian of Austria, passing the Low Countries to the Habsburg dynasty.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Belgium: From the cloth towns of Flanders to the heart of Europe, a young kingdom carved from the old Low Countries.", terralore.co/country/BEL/chronicle#ev-1477-the-habsburg-inheritance, claim TL:BEL:event:1477:the-habsburg-inheritance, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Abdication of Charles V in Brussels
claims.summary: The emperor Charles V, born in Ghent, abdicated the Netherlands to his son Philip II in Brussels in 1555, and the provinces passed under the rule of Habsburg Spain.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Belgium: From the cloth towns of Flanders to the heart of Europe, a young kingdom carved from the old Low Countries.", terralore.co/country/BEL/chronicle#ev-1555-abdication-of-charles-v-in-brussels, claim TL:BEL:event:1555:abdication-of-charles-v-in-brussels, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Union of Arras and the split of the Low Countries
claims.summary: The Catholic southern provinces reaffirmed loyalty to Spain in the Union of Arras while the northern provinces formed the Union of Utrecht, beginning the permanent division of the Low Countries into Belgium and the Netherlands.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Belgium: From the cloth towns of Flanders to the heart of Europe, a young kingdom carved from the old Low Countries.", terralore.co/country/BEL/chronicle#ev-1579-union-of-arras-and-the-split-of-the-low, claim TL:BEL:event:1579:union-of-arras-and-the-split-of-the-low, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Fall of Antwerp
claims.summary: After a siege of over a year, the Spanish commander Alessandro Farnese took the great Protestant port of Antwerp, confirming Spanish control of the southern Netherlands and driving its merchants and craftsmen north.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Belgium: From the cloth towns of Flanders to the heart of Europe, a young kingdom carved from the old Low Countries.", terralore.co/country/BEL/chronicle#ev-1585-fall-of-antwerp, claim TL:BEL:event:1585:fall-of-antwerp, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: From Spanish to Austrian Netherlands
claims.summary: By the Treaty of Utrecht ending the War of the Spanish Succession, the southern Netherlands passed from Spain to the Austrian Habsburgs, becoming the Austrian Netherlands.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Belgium: From the cloth towns of Flanders to the heart of Europe, a young kingdom carved from the old Low Countries.", terralore.co/country/BEL/chronicle#ev-1713-from-spanish-to-austrian-netherlands, claim TL:BEL:event:1713:from-spanish-to-austrian-netherlands, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: French annexation of the southern Netherlands
claims.summary: Revolutionary France annexed the Austrian Netherlands and the prince-bishopric of Liège, ending Habsburg rule and governing the region directly from Paris for twenty years.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Belgium: From the cloth towns of Flanders to the heart of Europe, a young kingdom carved from the old Low Countries.", terralore.co/country/BEL/chronicle#ev-1795-french-annexation-of-the-southern-netherlands, claim TL:BEL:event:1795:french-annexation-of-the-southern-netherlands, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Union with the Netherlands
claims.summary: After Napoleon's defeat at Waterloo on Belgian soil, the Congress of Vienna merged the southern provinces with the Dutch into the United Kingdom of the Netherlands under William I, as a buffer against France.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Belgium: From the cloth towns of Flanders to the heart of Europe, a young kingdom carved from the old Low Countries.", terralore.co/country/BEL/chronicle#ev-1815-union-with-the-netherlands, claim TL:BEL:event:1815:union-with-the-netherlands, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Belgian Revolution
claims.summary: Rebellion in Brussels drove out the Dutch garrison; a National Congress proclaimed independence and adopted a liberal constitution, breaking the southern provinces away from the United Kingdom of the Netherlands.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Belgium: From the cloth towns of Flanders to the heart of Europe, a young kingdom carved from the old Low Countries.", terralore.co/country/BEL/chronicle#ev-1830-the-belgian-revolution, claim TL:BEL:event:1830:the-belgian-revolution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Leopold I, first King of the Belgians
claims.summary: The German prince Leopold of Saxe-Coburg was installed as the first king and took his constitutional oath on 21 July 1831, a date still observed as Belgium's national day.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Belgium: From the cloth towns of Flanders to the heart of Europe, a young kingdom carved from the old Low Countries.", terralore.co/country/BEL/chronicle#ev-1831-leopold-i-first-king-of-the-belgians, claim TL:BEL:event:1831:leopold-i-first-king-of-the-belgians, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Treaty of London guarantees Belgian neutrality
claims.summary: Austria, Britain, France, Prussia, Russia and the Netherlands recognised Belgium as an independent and perpetually neutral state and guaranteed its neutrality, the treaty later cited by Britain to enter the First World War.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Belgium: From the cloth towns of Flanders to the heart of Europe, a young kingdom carved from the old Low Countries.", terralore.co/country/BEL/chronicle#ev-1839-treaty-of-london-guarantees-belgian-neutrality, claim TL:BEL:event:1839:treaty-of-london-guarantees-belgian-neutrality, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Accession of Leopold II
claims.summary: Leopold II succeeded Leopold I as King of the Belgians, ruling an industrialising kingdom while pursuing his own colonial ambitions in central Africa.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Belgium: From the cloth towns of Flanders to the heart of Europe, a young kingdom carved from the old Low Countries.", terralore.co/country/BEL/chronicle#ev-1865-accession-of-leopold-ii, claim TL:BEL:event:1865:accession-of-leopold-ii, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Foundation of the Congo Free State
claims.summary: After winning recognition at the Berlin Conference, Leopold II proclaimed the Congo Free State as his private possession, a regime whose forced labour and atrocities caused massive loss of life.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Belgium: From the cloth towns of Flanders to the heart of Europe, a young kingdom carved from the old Low Countries.", terralore.co/country/BEL/chronicle#ev-1885-foundation-of-the-congo-free-state, claim TL:BEL:event:1885:foundation-of-the-congo-free-state, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Annexation of the Congo by Belgium
claims.summary: Under international pressure over the atrocities, Leopold II was forced to cede his private colony to the Belgian state, which took it over as the Belgian Congo.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Belgium: From the cloth towns of Flanders to the heart of Europe, a young kingdom carved from the old Low Countries.", terralore.co/country/BEL/chronicle#ev-1908-annexation-of-the-congo-by-belgium, claim TL:BEL:event:1908:annexation-of-the-congo-by-belgium, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Neutral Moresnet
claims.summary: Unable to agree on ownership of a village and its zinc mine, the powers created Neutral Moresnet, a tiny condominium of about 3.5 square kilometres jointly administered by Prussia and the Netherlands, then Prussia and Belgium, until the Treaty of Versailles awarded it to Belgium.

sources.label: 100 years ago Belgium annexed Europe's second smallest territory (Neutral Moresnet)

claims.title: The Baarle enclaves take shape
claims.summary: Medieval land deals between the lords of Breda and the dukes of Brabant scattered sovereignty across Baarle, leaving the Belgian Baarle-Hertog as a cluster of enclaves inside the Netherlands, some containing Dutch counter-enclaves.

sources.label: Baarle-Hertog and Baarle-Nassau: the enclave complex

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Belgium: From the cloth towns of Flanders to the heart of Europe, a young kingdom carved from the old Low Countries.", terralore.co/country/BEL/chronicle#ev-1198-the-baarle-enclaves-take-shape, claim TL:BEL:event:1198:the-baarle-enclaves-take-shape, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Germany invades neutral Belgium
claims.summary: Executing the Schlieffen Plan, Germany invaded Belgium after King Albert I refused free passage; the violation of the 1839 neutrality treaty, dismissed as a 'scrap of paper', brought Britain into the First World War.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Belgium: From the cloth towns of Flanders to the heart of Europe, a young kingdom carved from the old Low Countries.", terralore.co/country/BEL/chronicle#ev-1914-germany-invades-neutral-belgium, claim TL:BEL:event:1914:germany-invades-neutral-belgium, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Battle of the Yser
claims.summary: Falling back behind the river Yser, the Belgian army opened the sluices and flooded the polders to halt the German advance, holding a last strip of free Belgium around Nieuwpoort and Diksmuide for the rest of the war.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Belgium: From the cloth towns of Flanders to the heart of Europe, a young kingdom carved from the old Low Countries.", terralore.co/country/BEL/chronicle#ev-1914-the-battle-of-the-yser, claim TL:BEL:event:1914:the-battle-of-the-yser, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Versailles: Eupen-Malmedy and the end of Moresnet
claims.summary: The Treaty of Versailles ended Belgian neutrality, abolished Neutral Moresnet and transferred Eupen, Malmedy and Sankt Vith from Germany to Belgium, giving the kingdom a German-speaking minority after a much-criticised popular consultation in 1920.

sources.publisher: 1914-1918-Online International Encyclopedia of the First World War

claims.title: Second German invasion
claims.summary: Germany again invaded neutral Belgium on 10 May 1940, this time thrusting through the Ardennes, and rapidly overwhelmed the defending Belgian, French and British forces.

sources.label: German Invasion of Western Europe, May 1940

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Belgium: From the cloth towns of Flanders to the heart of Europe, a young kingdom carved from the old Low Countries.", terralore.co/country/BEL/chronicle#ev-1940-second-german-invasion, claim TL:BEL:event:1940:second-german-invasion, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Surrender of King Leopold III
claims.summary: After eighteen days of fighting Leopold III surrendered the Belgian army without consulting his government, beginning four years of German occupation and a political crisis over the king's conduct.

sources.label: German Invasion of Western Europe, May 1940

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Belgium: From the cloth towns of Flanders to the heart of Europe, a young kingdom carved from the old Low Countries.", terralore.co/country/BEL/chronicle#ev-1940-surrender-of-king-leopold-iii, claim TL:BEL:event:1940:surrender-of-king-leopold-iii, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding member of NATO
claims.summary: Belgium was one of twelve states that signed the North Atlantic Treaty in Washington on 4 April 1949; NATO headquarters later moved to Brussels in 1967.

sources.label: 75 years of NATO: An Alliance firmly rooted in Belgium
sources.publisher: Focus on Belgium (Federal Government of Belgium)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Belgium: From the cloth towns of Flanders to the heart of Europe, a young kingdom carved from the old Low Countries.", terralore.co/country/BEL/chronicle#ev-1949-founding-member-of-nato, claim TL:BEL:event:1949:founding-member-of-nato, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding the European Community
claims.summary: Belgium was one of the six founders of the European Coal and Steel Community in 1951 and the European Economic Community by the Treaty of Rome in 1957, with Brussels becoming the centre of European integration.

sources.label: 75 years of NATO: An Alliance firmly rooted in Belgium
sources.publisher: Focus on Belgium (Federal Government of Belgium)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Belgium: From the cloth towns of Flanders to the heart of Europe, a young kingdom carved from the old Low Countries.", terralore.co/country/BEL/chronicle#ev-1957-founding-the-european-community, claim TL:BEL:event:1957:founding-the-european-community, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence of the Congo
claims.summary: The Belgian Congo became the independent Democratic Republic of the Congo, ending Belgium's central African colony amid turmoil and a swift descent into crisis.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Belgium: From the cloth towns of Flanders to the heart of Europe, a young kingdom carved from the old Low Countries.", terralore.co/country/BEL/chronicle#ev-1960-independence-of-the-congo, claim TL:BEL:event:1960:independence-of-the-congo, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The linguistic frontier fixed
claims.summary: Language laws drew a fixed border between Dutch-, French- and German-speaking areas and created four language regions, entrenching the divide between Belgium's communities.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Belgium: From the cloth towns of Flanders to the heart of Europe, a young kingdom carved from the old Low Countries.", terralore.co/country/BEL/chronicle#ev-1962-the-linguistic-frontier-fixed, claim TL:BEL:event:1962:the-linguistic-frontier-fixed, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Belgium becomes a federal state
claims.summary: The fourth state reform amended the constitution to declare Belgium a federal state composed of Communities and Regions, completing the devolution of the once-unitary kingdom.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Belgium: From the cloth towns of Flanders to the heart of Europe, a young kingdom carved from the old Low Countries.", terralore.co/country/BEL/chronicle#ev-1993-belgium-becomes-a-federal-state, claim TL:BEL:event:1993:belgium-becomes-a-federal-state, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
